correctness.rationale: Put m=n+1 and v_i=e_i−1/m on the sum-zero space H. The frame operator of the v_i is I_H. For u_i=Tv_i with unit circumradius, tr(TᵀT)=m. The opposite facet has distance 1/(m||T⁻ᵀv_i||), since ⟨v_j,v_i⟩=−1/m for j≠i. With A=(n/m)TᵀT the resulting traces are n and 1/(nh²) for A and A⁻¹, and the normalized volume is √det A. At h=1/n, equality in the reciprocal-trace Cauchy–Schwarz inequality forces A=I. Otherwise the spectral feasible set is compact away from zero and the two gradients are independent. Stationarity for log determinant gives a quadratic in each eigenvalue. With roots x>y the Lagrangian Hessian is negative at x and positive at y. A difference of two coordinate directions for a repeated root is tangent to both constraints; the second-order necessary condition rules out repeated x at a minimum and repeated y at a maximum. The eigenvalue ratios y/x=t² and exceptional multiplicity one give h⁻²=n²+(n−1)(1/t−t)² and the printed product formulas. For actual attainment, a balanced unit sign vector q∈H has |⟨q,v_i⟩|²=1/m for every i. Thus the two deformations along its rank-one projection preserve vertex uniformity and, using their inverses, facet-distance uniformity. In every equality case equal vertex lengths force these same coordinate squares, and any balanced signs differ only by permutation, giving congruence by the polar decomposition. As h↓0, t∼√(n−1)h gives both constants and powers. An independent arithmetic check at n=5,t=1/2 gives h⁻²=34 and the stated extremal trace pairs; the supplied rational Gram checker was inspected, not executed.
